Ganesh Narayanan: 
Thank you, Abhijit. A very good evening, everyone, and a very warm welcome to discuss our 
second quarter and first half of FY27 business performance.  
                                                We reported our highest quarterly profit of INR 502 Crore in this quarter, having grown fivefold 
over the past 5 years. Current financial year marks a clear turnaround, recording INR 995 Crore 
PAT in the first half as against INR 778 Crore PAT during the previous financial year. Our H1 
ROA stood at 5.9% and ROE stood at 23.8%. We are delivering record profitability while 
remaining amongst the most competitively priced lenders across our product segments. Our 
lending franchise today spans across Group Loans, Individual Business Loans, secured business 
loans, affordable housing loans and 2-wheeler finance, with growth, margins and asset quality 
all moving in the right direction. 
 
Our AUM grew 19.5% YoY and 2.1% QoQ to INR 30,946 Crore. Disbursements stood at INR 
6,355 Crore, up 19.4% YoY and 4.1% QoQ, taking H1 disbursements to INR 12,461 Crore. We 
added 2.3 Lakh new borrowers, of which 35% were new-to-credit, taking our H1 additions to 
4.9 Lakh customers. We also opened 60 new branches during the quarter, expanding our network 
to 2,326 branches across 460 districts. Digital collections rose to 26.3% versus 18.1% a year 
ago.  
                                                When we began building our retail franchise, our thesis was very simple. The customers we've 
served for years would need more than a Group Loan as their economic profile improves and 
financing needs expand. That thesis continues to play out at scale with regulatory support in 
place. Of the ~45 Lakh borrower base, 15% or 6.8 Lakh borrowers belong to Retail Finance.

Retail Finance AUM grew to INR 7,200 Crore, now 23.3% of the total AUM, up from 20.6% in 
Q1 FY27. Within this, our secured book comprising of Secured Business Loans, Affordable 
Housing Loans and 2-Wheeler Loans grew 60.9% YoY to INR 695 Crore. Our mortgage 
presence now spans across 300 GL and 128 Retail Finance branches with 2-wheeler loans 
offered through 950-plus Group Loan branches. Our 2-Wheeler Loan book witnessed strong 
traction, having crossed INR 60 Crore compared to INR 20 Crore in Q1. Further, our ability to 
meet evolving credit needs of our customers is also deepening their loyalty with borrower 
retention rates improving from 85% in FY26 to 88% in H1 FY27. Alongside, we are also 
strengthening our collection ability with a dedicated collection team comprising of 500-plus 
employees across operating geographies.  
                                                Our Group Loan portfolio stood at INR 23,746 Crore as of September 2026, a marginal decline 
of 2% from the start of FY27. This was on account of write-offs and graduation. Most of the 
INR 614 Crore portfolio written-off in H1 FY27 consisted of Group Loans. With write-offs 
normalizing and the seasonally stronger second half ahead and increase in customer acquisition 
during H2, we expect the Group Loan book growth to return to guided levels. 
 
Commenting on our asset quality, we saw a temporary increase in monthly PAR accretion rate 
during August and September, driven by excess rainfall and flooding in certain regions of Bihar, 
UP, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh, along with seasonal festivities in a few geographies. 
However, despite this, our asset quality is back to pre-crisis levels at its best in the last 10 
quarters. 
 
Gross NPA stood at 1.79%, net NPA at 0.59% and PAR 90 plus at 1.11%, each improving 
sequentially. collection efficiency, excluding arrears, stood at 97.9% and X-Bucket collection 
efficiency for September stood at 99.71%. Credit cost for the quarter stood at INR 299 Crore or 
0.99% on a non-annualized basis, of which 70 bps was driven by new PAR and 29 bps due to 
increasing ECL provisioning rates. We further strengthened our ECL provisioning at 3.31% after 
building a macroprudential buffer of 45 bps or INR 137 Crore. Our annualized H1 FY27 credit 
cost of 3.43% includes normative credit cost of 2.98% and 0.45% of macroprudential buffer, 
which is well within our guided range.  
                                                Commenting on our margins, we saw our NIM expand to 15.1% in Q2 from 14.4% in Q1, driven 
by lower interest reversals in Group Loan book, higher yielding individual loan book, stable cost 
of borrowing and higher capital push. Our cost-to-income ratio improved to 28.2% and PPOP 
grew 39.6% YoY and 11.2% QoQ to INR 970 Crore in Q2 FY27. Our marginal cost of 
borrowing stood at 9.1% in Q2 FY27, while average cost of borrowing was stable at 9.1%. Our 
capital position strengthened further with our capital adequacy at 26.9%, Tier 1 at 26.2% and 
total equity base of INR 8,919 Crore.  
                                                On the liability side, diversifying our funding mix, coupled with focus on long tenure funds 
remains our medium-term strategy. We signed USD 175 million ECB loan in October, 
syndicated by Standard Chartered Bank and DBS Bank. Despite global macroeconomic 
uncertainty and strong competition in the ECB market from FCNR (B) deposit mobilization by 
banks, the transaction received a strong response at a competitive pricing with financial 
institutions participating from across Asia, Middle East and Africa. We see this as a clear

NCDs help us both in liability diversification as well as securing longer tenure of funding to 
strengthen our ALM. 
 
Basis our strong H1 FY27 financial performance. We raised our profitability guidance for FY27, 
ROA of 5.2% to 5.8% versus 4% to 4.8% earlier and ROE of 21% to 24% versus 16% to 20% 
earlier. We retain our AUM growth guidance of 20% to 25%, supported by return to growth in 
Group Loan portfolio, coupled with continued momentum in Retail Finance.  
                                                We expect a NIM of 14.4% to 14.7% as against 12.8% to 13.2% guided earlier, driven by healthy 
asset quality, strong control over borrowing costs and a higher capital position even after 
factoring the 50-bps rate reduction applicable from October onwards. We are best placed to 
protect our NIMs in an evolving macroeconomic environment. Our risk-adjusted NIMs are 
currently at highest levels. Further, we can maintain our borrowing cost range bound, supported 
by diversified lender base, high-quality PSL book and judicious borrowing mix between repo, 
MCLR and fixed rates. Cost to income may range between 29% to 30% as operating costs remain 
well under control, despite inflationary trends.  
                                                We're maintaining our credit cost guidance of 3% to 4%, and it should comfortably cover for 
any volatility on account of evolving drought-related conditions in some operating geographies. 
We are seeing a few signs of drought-related challenges in October around certain pockets of 
Maharashtra, wherein the borrowers are requesting for additional time for repayment, including 
restructuring options. At this point of time, we're not seeing any on-ground impact in any other 
geographies. We also note that Northeast monsoons are expected to be normal, providing respite 
to Southern Peninsula India. 
 
We'll focus on addressing the growing credit needs of our established seasoned customers with 
a proven track record and record of repayment across credit cycles through renewals, Group 
Loan servicing and targeted graduation to individual secured lending products. New customer 
acquisition will be a key growth driver with momentum expected to accelerate in H2. 
 
To conclude, CA Grameen today is stronger, more diversified and more profitable than any point 
in its history, and we are executing with the discipline of a franchise that has been tested through 
cycles. As we enter the seasonally stronger second half, we do so with momentum in our 
business, strengthen our balance sheet and full confidence in delivering the guidance we've set 
out today.
